_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1257's FRESHNESS PASS IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
WHAT THE PASS IS. `scripts/verify.sh --fresh` removes the build artifacts of
every package the working tree has changed against HEAD, in the workspace the
command it precedes is about to build. That is R743's RECOVERY half — the
flock stops two cargo runs from corrupting one build directory, and this is
what gets a tree back after one already did. Until this round it was shell
asking git about `crates/` and running `cargo clean -p <directory name>`,
which are two statements about the ROOT workspace in a repository with
EACH INJECTION IS A WAY THE PASS STOPS BEING ONE WHILE STILL LOOKING LIKE
ONE. None of them prints an error, none is red anywhere else, and every one
of them leaves a run whose green verdict is about artifacts nobody removed.
Scoped to this crate's own suite: nothing here touches the tree it acts on,
so running the repository's whole suite would be minutes of proving nothing.

injections.name: the-population-is-the-root-workspaces-directory-again
injections.why: N139 itself, put back. `crates/` is where the ROOT workspace's members live, so a population shaped like that directory is silent about `bench/`, `studio/` and every `tools/*` — twenty-three workspaces whose suites run through this wrapper. Nothing goes red anywhere else and no message changes: the pass reports a smaller number of changed packages, which reads exactly like a tree that changed fewer

injections.name: the-workspace-freshened-is-always-the-root-one
injections.why: the other half of the same defect and the quieter one. `cargo clean -p` acts on the workspace it is pointed at, so a pass that ignores the command's own `--manifest-path` asks the ROOT workspace about a package it has never heard of. The clean then fails, and a pass that discarded that status — as the shell's `|| true` did — is a no-op with a green exit

injections.name: the-pass-asks-for-members-rather-than-for-the-resolve
injections.why: a workspace's MEMBERS are not the code its suite compiles. Six workspaces under `tools/` path-depend on `tools/ci-plan`, which is a member of the ROOT workspace and of none of theirs, so `--no-deps` reports `0 packages changed` for every one of them on a round that edited `ci-plan` — while the suite about to run is the one that compiles it. The direction is the quiet one: a smaller number, no message, a faster pass

injections.name: the-repository-boundary-is-dropped-from-the-resolve
injections.why: reading a resolve with dependencies also reaches every registry crate and, for `studio`, a sibling checkout this repository does not own. None of them can ever be SELECTED — a changed path comes from git here and cannot be inside them — so what the boundary moves is the number printed beside the selection. `0 of 400` says nothing about whether this pass read anything, which is the one thing that number is for

injections.name: the-clean-pins-whatever-workspace-it-is-aimed-at
injections.why: a free resolve REWRITES a lockfile it disagrees with, which is what `locked_resolution_smoke` exists for, and pinning a workspace this repository does not own is a gate that goes red for somebody else's commit. `check-side-workspaces.sh` decides that once and puts the answer on the command; a pass that decided again would be a second answer to it, and this is what the wrong one looks like

injections.name: an-untracked-file-is-not-a-difference-from-head
injections.why: `git diff HEAD` answers about tracked files, so a module added to a crate and not committed leaves that crate's artifacts in place — and what they are artifacts OF is a version of the crate that no longer exists. It is the direction that reads as a working pass: fewer packages to clean, no message, a faster run

injections.name: a-workspace-cargo-cannot-read-becomes-a-pass-with-nothing-to-do
injections.why: the one answer that must not be quiet. A pass that could not find out which packages a workspace has has NOT RUN, and a caller that reads that as `nothing to clean` goes on to verify with whatever artifacts the tree already had. The old shell had exactly this shape twice over — `2>/dev/null` on the question and `|| true` on the act

injections.name: the-clean-is-decided-and-not-run
injections.why: the decision and the act are two things, and only one of them is what a reader sees. A pass that prints `cleaning side-crate`, records `ran cargo clean -p side-crate`, exits 0 and removes nothing is indistinguishable from a working one everywhere except in cargo's build directory — which is the one place the run that follows reads

injections.name: the-shallowest-package-owns-a-changed-file
injections.why: a workspace root can itself be a package with members below it — `tools/injection-harness` and `tools/experiment-harness` are that shape here — so a changed file is inside TWO member directories and exactly one of them compiles it. Picking the shallower one cleans a package that did not change and leaves the artifacts of the one that did: a wasted rebuild AND a stale binary, from one comparison
